mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near its current level or rises from the recent plateau, commuting-linked foot traffic will support higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace mobility weakens or if retail remains detached from commuting activity.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is less negative than RETAIL_REC and has held near -21 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior 28 days even though WORKPLACES remains above -25 and TRANSIT does not fall further.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS above the recent baseline signals warmer-outdoor leisure demand that spills into nearby retail visits within one to two weeks. The effect fails if the parks increase is isolated and does not coincide with broader outdoor activity.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to nonnegative week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -15.6 to 2.3 then back negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean after PARKS turns nonnegative and stays there for at least one week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while TRANSIT remains suppressed, people substitute local shopping for longer trips, which lifts retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks. The hypothesis fails if high residential time does not translate into more local errands.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive across all four weeks while TRANSIT remains around -28 to -31
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +8 and TRANSIT staying below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its current range indicates tighter movement constraints or weaker public-transport usage, which should depress retail and recreation mobility within one week. The mechanism fails if transit falls but retail does not follow downward.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 after being above -29
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved to -26.1 then returned to about -28
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior week after TRANSIT crosses below -30.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM becomes less negative while RETAIL_REC remains weak, routine errand substitution will keep discretionary retail from rebounding over the next two weeks. This mechanism fails when grocery mobility weakens or retail begins to decouple upward.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near -2 to -6 while RETAIL_REC stayed near -20 to -26
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average while GROCERY_PHARM remains around or above -5.

mechanism_narrative: A broad improvement in PARKS combined with higher RESIDENTIAL time signals spring outdoor substitution away from indoor shopping, pulling retail and recreation mobility lower over the next four weeks. The effect fails if outdoor use does not coincide with more time at home.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS briefly turned positive at t-2w while RESIDENTIAL stayed near +9 to +10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS is nonnegative or rising and RESIDENTIAL stays above +8.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both weaken together after this date, the combined commuting signal will reduce discretionary retail visits within four weeks. The hypothesis fails when one mobility channel falls but the other offsets it.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops more than 2 points week-on-week and TRANSIT drops more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stayed materially below baseline in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 28 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT post simultaneous week-on-week declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained lift in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent range indicates more routine out-of-home errands, which should spill over into retail and recreation mobility within one week. The mechanism fails if grocery trips rise without any retail follow-through.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 after spending at least two weeks below -3
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved to -2.0 at t-2w before easing to -3.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within one week after GROCERY_PHARM moves above -2.
